Deploy-Bot: 3167890123 Canary rollout started for service=prompt-router image=prompt-router:v6. Targeting 10% traffic in prod (feature flag routing_v6_canary enabled for the slice). Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4823
IncBot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate detected on prompt-router canary in prod. Trigger at 3167890145 -> current canary error rate 12% (baseline ~0.5%). Paging on-call SRE.
Emma (oncall): I'm on it, looking at logs and traces. First check: topology and recent rollouts. @Maria can you confirm which flag gate controls the new route?
Maria (SRE): Confirmed: routing_v6_canary (backed by routing_v6 variants). Canary slice = 10% prod traffic from staging2 path. Pulling traces now.
Ben (eng): Seeing a lot of KV-cache misses and connection churn in the canary pods. Also token-p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~980ms. Repro script suggests header mismatch on some client paths.
Emma (oncall): Customer impact? Tina, any CS tickets yet?
Tina (Customer-Success): Just got the first ticket from Acme — timeouts in chat flows. Opening incident ticket and notifying affected accounts (acme, novahealth).
Emma (oncall): We need to remove canary traffic immediately. Lia, can you toggle the FF to stop routing_v6_canary in prod?
Lia (infra): Running toggle now.
Lia (infra): ```
redwood-ff toggle routing_v6_canary --env=prod --value=false --reason="emergency canary spike"
```
Lia (infra): Command returned: {"result":"ok","changed":"routing_v6_canary=false","ts":3167890201}
Emma (oncall): :white_check_mark: Flag flipped. Observing metrics — error rate beginning to drop but still elevated. Maria, can we snap traffic back to stable and scale canary to 0?
Maria (SRE): Executing snapback steps:
```
kubectl scale deploy prompt-router-canary --replicas=0 -n prod
redwood-router set-slice prompt-router stable=100 canary=0
```
Maria (SRE): Scale and slice update completed at 3167890265. Routing now on stable=100%.
Deploy-Bot: Canary pods terminated gracefully, fallback route active.
Tina (Customer-Success): CS update sent to Acme & Novahealth. Initial guidance: retry after 60s, limit parallel streams. Creating support tickets.
Emma (oncall): Impact window estimate? Maria?
Maria (SRE): Affected window ~3167890145-3167890220 (≈75s). Total affected requests ~24k, peak error rate 14%. Latency tail returned to baseline ~40s after flag flip. No evidence of data loss.
Ben (eng): Preliminary root cause: routing_v6 variant expects an extra header that some staging2-originated requests don't include, leading to downstream connection churn and cache thrash. We can repro in staging2 with the repro script: https://runbook/internal/repro/routing_v6
Lia (infra): Mitigations in place: flag disabled, canary scaled to 0, and an emergency policy added to limit auto-retries >3 for prompt-router to reduce amplification. Also pinning the rollout in the deployment controller.
Emma (oncall): Handoff: @Maria you'll own the timeline + postmortem doc, @Ben you own the RCA and patch plan, @Tina you own customer comms and impacted accounts. I'll stay on-call for escalation.
Maria (SRE): Acknowledged. Creating postmortem doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/3167890123 (initializing timeline, logs, and dtrace snippets).
Tina (Customer-Success): Notifying account teams and drafting customer-safe explanation. ETA for outbound message 30m.
Ben (eng): Plan: revert the routing header expectation in prompt-router v6 or make it backward-compatible, add an integration test for header-less clients, and run a canary in a restricted slice.
Emma (oncall): Closing pager - we moved traffic off the canary and error rate returned near baseline. Continue investigation in thread and update the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
IncBot: Incident annotated: "FF-induced canary failure -> emergency prune/snapback". Severity: Sev2. Pager resolved at 3167890800.
